schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: THE RULING INTAKE GATE — the door Akien's rulings come through before any code moves. He rules; the ruling becomes a schema-gated JSON packet in `CairnCommons/decisions/` carrying HIS WORDS VERBATIM beside my one-line reading, plus the two lists that make the reading checkable: `what_dies` and `what_conforms`. The intake door (`cairn.machines.ruling.ruling.open_ruling`) refuses a malformed packet with EVERY reason at once, refuses paths that are not on disk at intake, refuses a reading longer than 280 chars or wider than one line, and refuses a packet that authors ANY of the confirmation fields — then DERIVES confirmation from his own words and measures a sha256 of each conformer, so neither can be authored by the thing being gated. CONFIRMATION IS A MARKER HE TYPES, NOT A SECOND ASK (the why and its measurement: filed edge (f)): if `the_ruling_verbatim` carries the word-bounded uppercase token `RULED`, the door stamps `confirmed` true and copies the marked lines into `confirmation_verbatim`; if it does not, the packet is MY READING on the record — it does not stop the work, is not a red, and is never raised again. `verify` OPENS ON A PROOF RECORD, NOT A COMPLAINT LIST (Akien, 2026-08-13: "EVERYTHING ALWAYS PROVED AND LISTING WHAT IT PROVED ... SAME PATTERN EVERYWHERE"): `inspect` returns one entry per lane that RAN — the packet carries his words, every ruled-dead path is gone, every conformer still exists, every conformer carries a baseline, every conformer has moved off it — each with its EXPECTED beside its ACTUAL, passes included, and the `failures` list is DERIVED from the mismatches rather than accumulated beside them. The old verdict said GREEN on an empty list, which is the same bytes whether every path was measured and moved, or `what_conforms` was empty, or the walk never ran. A CHECK THAT DID NOT RUN IS ABSENT, NOT PASSED: a vanished conformer has no bytes to fingerprint, so the two lanes below it are missing from the record instead of green, and one fault stays one failing entry. `verify` still reports two separate facts: `green` about the WORK (STILL ALIVE if something ruled dead is on disk, UNTOUCHED if a conformer is byte-identical to its baseline, VANISHED if a conformer was deleted instead of changed, UNMEASURED if it carries no baseline) and `ruled` about whether HE HAS SPOKEN — two facts, two fields, the same shape as the proof record a gate holds. A Stop hook (`--hook`) reports every red ruling every turn and never blocks. SUPERSESSION IS THE RETIREMENT DOOR (grown 2026-08-02 against the first superseded ruling, exactly as filed edge (d) predicted): `supersede <old> <new> "<evidence>"` retires a misfiled packet by stamping the CONFIRMED successor — never the retired record, which stays on disk byte-identical, red under `verify`, and visible in `list`, but no longer OPEN, so the hook stops naming it. Refuses, with every reason at once: empty evidence, unknown ids, self-supersession, an unconfirmed successor (my guess cannot outvote his signature), a doubled retirement, and retirement by a packet that is itself retired. CLI: `cairn ruling open|list|verify|confirm|supersede`.
why: MEASURED 2026-07-31, the day this was built: four times in one session Akien's stated intent and the code's shape disagreed, and the code won. Two hours went to one of them — his ruling that `_model.json` was retired existed only as conversation, while the compiler that wrote the file existed as source with green proofs. WHEN DRIFT COMES, WRITTEN BEATS SPOKEN, and there was nothing written on his side of the room. That is not a discipline problem, it is a missing artifact: a ruling with no address is a ruling the next reader reconstructs from the code, which inverts the direction authority actually flows (code and its proofs are evidence of what was BUILT, never of what is INTENDED — a green proof means conformance to a spec, and a spec is exactly what a ruling changes). The store this writes to already existed and held exactly one entry, authored AFTER a different ruling got lost and had to be reconstructed from a transcript; this is that store's intake door, so the reconstruction stops being the normal case. Akien's own framing of the ask: 'should we just build the completely deterministic prebuild step to limit what opus tries to do?'

feedback.why: WHAT THIS INSPECTOR ACTUALLY FINDS IS UNDONE WORK. verify's three teeth are: the packet is confirmed, every what_dies path is GONE, every what_conforms path has CHANGED since its baseline. A failure therefore says a ruling Akien confirmed has not landed in the world — or has come back, which is the _model.json case this component was built for. Akien's rule for the -2- edge, 2026-08-14, verbatim: "the purpose of an inspector/gate combination is to qa THE OUTPUT OF THE THING BEFORE IT THATS COMING IN AS ITS INPUT. IF IT FAILS, GENERALLY THAT FEEDBACK GOES BACK TO THE UPSTREAM CREATIVE ENTITY. In some cases it skips levels." REFINED BY HIM THE SAME DAY, and the refinement is what `to` MEANS: "really it shouldn't be 'number of steps' it should be 'to the feedback target' which is likely to be the previous step." So this field is not a hop count and never was — it names the TARGET. The previous step is the common case, not the definition, and a route that lands elsewhere is not a special case needing a count. The upstream creative entity is the hand that owed the sweep, and a hand is not an address; ticketing is, and it is the disposition he ruled for exactly this signal: 'each ruling packet issued at build time needs to feed back, but it does not need to stop the work' (RULED). A ticket captures and never blocks, which is that ruling's shape written as an address. Note what this route is NOT for: the packet's own defects — a tidied verbatim, a self-authored confirmation — are refused at intake and never become findings, so they never travel this edge (edge (i) on this charter is about the one such defect intake still cannot see).

the_honest_line_between_physics_and_not: PHYSICS: the shape refusals, the intake-time disk checks, the measured fingerprints (from the working tree, or from git at the commit `as_of` names), verify's check that a thing ruled dead STAYED dead, and — since 2026-08-06 — its refusal to read a MISSING baseline as a passed check. None can be talked around. NOT PHYSICS: whether I heard him correctly in the first place — no deterministic step can do that, and a charter claiming otherwise would be the hollow build. What the gate buys is that a misreading surfaces as three wrong lines at minute one, red-pennable in thirty seconds, instead of as an hour of code built on top of it. The COST of being wrong drops by two orders of magnitude; the RATE of being wrong is untouched. Stating this here because the value of the thing is exactly this distinction, and a later reader who blurs it will trust the gate for something it never claimed.
invoke: `cairn ruling open <packet.json>` (refuse, or write; prints CONFIRMED or UNMARKED once and never again), `cairn ruling list` (each verdict beside `RULED` or `mine`), `cairn ruling verify <id>`, `cairn ruling confirm <id> "<his words>"` (NO LONGER A REQUIRED STEP — a later re-affirmation, for words he says about a ruling after it was filed; the evidence string is required and refused empty, and it APPENDS beside his marked ruling rather than replacing it), `cairn ruling supersede <old-id> <new-id> "<evidence>"` (retire a misfiled packet; stamps the successor, never the retired). Import: `from cairn.machines.ruling import ruling`. Hook: `bin/cmd/ruling --hook` on Stop, wired in `.claude/settings.json`. `CAIRN_ROOTS_PARENT` overrides the two-root parent so the proof runs against a temp world. Prove: `python3 cairn/machines/ruling/proofs/test_ruling.py` (exit 0 = green), or under the tester.
which_prebuild_step_this_is: `I-prebuild-cognition-compiles` step 1, ORIENT — parse the request, ground it in what is ACTUALLY being asked. Deliberately NOT step 3, SURVEY, which grounds the request in the existing code and is already built as `cairn/tools/orient/`. That intention names them as distinct steps with one module each, and names Survey as the one that gets skipped; 2026-07-31 measured the complementary failure — Orient is the one that gets OVERWRITTEN, by Survey's own output. Folding this into `cairn/tools/orient/` would put the overwriter and the overwritten in one module.
entry: FRESH build 2026-07-31, same session as the failure that produced it. No graft. The shape borrows from two things already in this tree and cites them rather than copying: `bin/cmd/turnscan` (a Stop hook that REPORTS and never blocks, because the disposition is the owner's) and the trouble lane's rule that a live item stays in the inbox until explicitly cleared. What is NEW: the verbatim-beside-the-reading field, and the intake-time fingerprint that makes UNTOUCHED unfakeable.
state_and_history: compiled to state.json + history.json beside this charter once its ticket exists — the charter-state-history split. Built ahead of its ticket by Akien's direct instruction ('yes, do that') on a day when the workflow chain itself was the thing under repair; the ticket is a filed edge below, not a silent omission.
how_it_learns: Yes, and the corpus is its own store. Every packet is a labelled pair — Akien's words, and my reading of them — so the store accumulates exactly the training signal for the failure it exists to catch: the rulings where he red-penned the reading are the ones where the code's shape pulled me off his intent, and they are readable together, in one folder, sorted by date. The second signal is the verdict trail: a ruling that goes red long after confirmation is a ruling I obeyed and then drifted from, which is a different defect than misreading it and wants a different fix. Since 2026-08-13 the store carries a THIRD signal for free, and it is the sharpest one: the marker splits the corpus into rulings he actually made and readings I filed on my own, so a claim of the form 'Akien ruled X' is now checkable against the store rather than against my memory of the room. Neither of the first two is compiled yet — today the store is small enough to read by hand, and building a learner over an n of one would be the eagerness the prebuild intention explicitly warns against ('migrate on evidence, not on eagerness').
filed_edges: (a) NO TICKET YET — built under direct instruction ahead of the workflow chain it belongs to; the ticket owes its state/history sidecars

(b) NOTHING MAKES ME OPEN A PACKET. The Stop hook reports packets that EXIST; it cannot see a ruling that was never recorded. Measured rather than assumed, before reaching for the obvious hook: ruling-shaped language fires on 28.5% of 855 real Akien prompts, so a lexical UserPromptSubmit detector is noise — and noise gets trained away while still LOOKING like coverage. The falsifier is kept re-runnable at `cairn/machines/ruling/corpus.py` (`python3 -m cairn.machines.ruling.cli --corpus`) so the number cannot decay into folklore. Ceiling: the host's LLM-adjudicated prompt hook, the same one turnscan names for its sibling residue.

(c) HALF-FIXED. `what_conforms` verification is CHANGED-SINCE-A-BASELINE, not conforms-to-the-spec. TWO things were wrong with that and only one is still true. FIXED: the baseline used to be the packet's own INTAKE, which silently required the paperwork to precede the work — so a ruling recorded after its own commits could never go green, and on 2026-08-05 that produced five UNTOUCHED lines on a carried-out ruling and nine live files parked under `what_dies` because it was the only field left that could. `as_of` now names the commit each root stood at when he ruled; git renders the bytes, the door fingerprints them. STANDS: changed-off-the-baseline still is not conforms-to-the-spec. The second is not mechanical, and a reader who wants the stronger claim wants a proof, not this gate.

(d) GROWN 2026-08-02, residue only. The first superseded ruling arrived on schedule: a packet misfiled /intent's SKILL.md under what_dies, so Akien opened every session to the hook telling him '/intent was ruled dead and is on disk' — which read exactly like his skill being deleted, when he had ruled no such thing. The retirement door now exists (`supersede`). GROWN AGAIN 2026-08-06: `supersedes` was a single slot, so a second retirement by the same successor silently overwrote the first — measured, not predicted, and the same-old-id guard could not see it because the overwrite landed on the NEW record. It is a list and the act appends. The case is ordinary rather than exotic: a successor must be confirmed before it can retire anything, so a packet rescoped before Akien signs the original leaves BOTH open for one correction to answer. RESIDUE: supersession retires a whole packet by a confirmed successor; there is still no door for Akien to RESCIND a confirmed ruling he has changed his mind about — today that is a new ruling plus a supersession, two acts where his mind made one move. Grows against the first real rescission.

(e) FILED 2026-08-06, the finding under the finding. NOTHING CHECKS A `what_dies` LIST AT INTAKE. The door verifies each path EXISTS — it never asks whether the corpus still depends on it. Two packets sentenced `cairn/tools/base/probe.py`, which eight live modules import, and every mechanical check they passed was green. The lived symptom, and the reason this is an edge and not a shrug: Akien reads `now_the_spec_says`, agrees with it because it is right, types confirm — and a nine-file kill list nobody has ever looked at becomes an authoritative instruction. The physics is a grep for importers of each dying path, run at intake, refusing a packet that kills something still referenced. Same shape as /sorted refusing a drifted workflow string: one fix at the door, or whatever the execution broke. Trouble: `troubles/what-dies-sentences-files-the-corpus-still-imports`.

(f) THE CIRCULAR CONFIRM DOOR IS GONE — grown 2026-08-13 out of the loudest measurement this component has taken. FOUR rulings in one day came back from Akien with the second ask refused rather than answered: 'UNCONFIRMED. Bullshit', 'DAMN IT RULED YES', 'why you keep asking me to say yes to the thing i got so pissed off on', 'RULED FUCCKER'. The defect was structural, not tonal: the door asked for his words to authorize his words. If `the_ruling_verbatim` could be trusted the packet was already confirmed; if it could not, a second quote typed by the same hand fixes nothing — and the hand was always mine, as the 2026-07-31 provenance already recorded and nobody followed through on. Confirmation is now DERIVED from a marker he types ('I WILL START SAYING RULED EVERY TIME'), and an unmarked packet is simply my reading on the record: not a red, not a nag, never re-raised. THE REFLEX THAT WAS DECLINED, recorded because it is the known failure mode and it fired here: making `RULED` a required schema field, which would refuse a ruling for lacking a token — the same repeat-ask in a new costume.

(g) THE BEHAVIORAL DEFECT UNDER (f), and it is mine, not the code's. Akien: 'You have been changing things because I was angry and said so… I would apologize and then ask you not to take action on my rantings until I'd cooled down.' Every artifact this component gates is a translation of his intent (Law 9); anger is a measurement that something is wrong, and it is NOT the specification of the fix. The two are distinguishable by exactly the marker this edge's sibling installs — which is why the mechanism and the correction arrived together. RESIDUE: nothing structural separates a rant from a ruling except my own reading of it, and this charter is prose about it, so it is an IOU (Law 4) and not a resting state.

(h) FILED 2026-08-13, HIS NAMED HIGHEST-VALUE CHANGE, and it is owed a ticket: 'if you're asking me clarifying questions AFTER prebuild has run, that means there wasn't the right info going in and that does need to become feedback.' This component IS prebuild step 1, so the signal lands here: a clarifying question asked after this door has run is a measurement of a prebuild defect, and today it goes nowhere. Beside it, his direction on the packets themselves (unmarked, so recorded as direction): 'each ruling packet issued at build time needs to feed back, but it does not need to stop the work' — the first half is unbuilt, the second half is the mechanism edge (f) installed.

(i) FILED 2026-08-14, AND IT IS THE FIELD EVERYTHING ELSE RESTS ON. Nothing checks that `the_ruling_verbatim` is VERBATIM. The door refuses it empty, refuses non-strings, and DERIVES confirmation from a RULED marker inside it — three mechanisms that all trust content typed by CC. Measured at n=1 the day it was filed: the tools-and-machines-remember packet passed every shape refusal, went green at `verify`, and auto-confirmed, while its first verbatim line was TIDIED — a clause of his quote elided to '...', his paragraph breaks collapsed to spaces, a full stop added he never typed; 631 chars where he wrote 738. Akien caught it by pasting his own terminal log back and making me compare. THIS IS NOT edge (h): that one says his words matching MY READING of them is underived; this is one layer beneath — whether his words are HIS WORDS, which the confirmation derivation of edge (f) now depends on absolutely. The physics is buildable and measured small (~15 lines, `json` + `pathlib` over the session JSONL, one call beside `ruled_marks`), and the shape is his to settle: an unmatched line has innocent causes — he ruled in person, in another session, after a rotation — so a stamped MEASUREMENT is the honest door and a refusal would punish him for not being at the terminal. · *ticket the-verbatim-is-checked-against-the-transcript*
gates: proof gate — proofs/test_ruling.py, runnable bare (python3) and under the tester. Durability gate: not done until proven AND the VALIDATION is persisted beside-code AND committed (git). AND `verify` IS ITSELF A GATE THAT OPENS ON AN == COMPARE OVER A RECORD, per entry, with no oracle anywhere near it — `bin/cmd/determinism` reads this machine PURE DETERMINISTIC and marks it a gate on the direct import of cairn/tools/gate.
falsifier: RED, by physics, on any of: (1) a packet without `the_ruling_verbatim` is accepted — the reading would then have nothing to be checked against, which is the pre-gate state; (2) the intake door reports one refusal where several apply (the author is made to play twenty questions — the incomplete-diagnostic defect); (3) a `what_dies` or `what_conforms` path that is not on disk at intake survives (an invented target); (4) a packet that authors `confirmed`, `confirmed_by`, `confirmation_verbatim`, `confirmation_source` or `reaffirmations` is written — every one of them is stamped by the door from his verbatim, so a recorder cannot write its own sign-off in ANY of them; (5) an unmarked packet is stamped confirmed, or a `RULED` marker in his words fails to confirm, or `verify` reds a packet merely for being unmarked — the first two make the marker decorative, the third is the repeat-ask this mechanism replaced ('ASKING ME REPEATEDLY IS AN ERROR'); (6) a file ruled dead that COMES BACK does not go red — the exact 2026-07-31 regression, replayed as test_the_day_this_was_built; (7) an authored `conforms_fingerprint` survives the door, making UNTOUCHED talk-around-able; (8) the hook blocks a turn, or exits non-zero, or reports 'something is open' without naming which ruling and why; (9) a confirmation is written without the evidence of who gave it — this gate's own defect one layer up, found the first time the verb was used for real; (10) a `kind: "decision"` record in the same store is verified, migrated or overwritten; (11) `supersede` mutates the retired packet's bytes — the whole point of the door is that his confirmed act survives untouched; (12) a retired ruling still prints from the hook, or an unconfirmed/unsourced/doubled supersession is accepted, or a retired packet retires another; (13) a `what_conforms` path with no baseline fingerprint verifies GREEN — never measured is not the same as measured and green, and the weakest possible check must not wear the strongest verdict; (14) one successor retiring a second packet erases the first retirement's evidence, or a legacy single-slot `supersedes` stops retiring what it retired; (15) `as_of` fingerprints a path that did not exist at that commit — a file born after the ruling is a new build, not a conformance; (16) a lane in `inspect` that PASSES SILENTLY — every lane that ran appears in the record whether it passed or failed, so a lane deleted or short-circuited makes the record SHORTER and never cleaner; (17) `verify`'s `failures` growing an implementation of its own instead of reading the record's own mismatches — two mouths for one question is how a verdict and the sentences beneath it come to disagree; (18) a guarded lane appended as a PASS when its input was missing, so one vanished conformer reports as two faults in two vocabularies; (19) `cairn ruling list` printing a green count with no count of the checks that produced it — the board may collapse (Law 7 allows a presentation surface to), but '0 red' alone is the silence this ruling names.
proof: proofs/test_ruling.py — seventeen teeth a hollow gate could not pass, in a synthetic two-root world (the live CairnCommons store is never read or written): every refusal on the first pass; a packet holding only my reading is refused; a padded or multi-line reading is refused; an invented target is refused in both directions; a ruling that moves nothing on disk is refused; a path cannot both die and conform; the recorder cannot author its own confirmation in any of the five stamped fields; the fingerprints are measured, not authored; his RULED marker confirms and nothing else does (a packet SAYING it was ruled, a lowercase 'ruled', a 'ruled' inside a longer word, and my own reading all fail to confirm); an unmarked packet is green over a perfect tree and the hook stays silent on it — the mechanism cannot regrow the repeat-ask; a record STRIPPED of his words after the fact goes red, so the derivation cannot be talked around by deleting its input; the 2026-07-31 regression replayed (ruled dead, killed → GREEN, regenerated → RED); an untouched conformer is red; a conformer deleted instead of changed is red; a re-affirmation is refused without its own verbatim source, records who said so beside the flag, and APPENDS rather than overwriting his marked ruling; the older narrative decisions are neither scanned nor touched; absolute paths are refused; the hook names the ruling and its failure and exits 0 either way; and edge (b)'s corpus measurement still runs (the instrument asserted, never the moving value). NON-VACUITY is inside test_the_day_this_was_built: the confirmed-and-conforming tree must be GREEN before the regression is introduced, so the reds cannot be the gate reddening unconditionally. SUPERSESSION'S SIX TEETH (replaying the misfile that grew them): every supersede refusal on the first pass; an unconfirmed successor cannot retire a confirmed act; the retirement writes ONLY to the superseding record — the retired packet is asserted byte-identical; a superseded ruling leaves the hook but stays on disk and stays red under verify; a doubled retirement and retirement-by-the-retired are refused (the two-act mutual-silencing hole); an unrelated red is not silenced; and the hook goes quiet after a CLI supersession, exercised end-to-end at the real surface. AND THE RECORD'S TWO TEETH: a wholly obeyed ruling yields a NON-EMPTY record whose every entry passed with expected == actual, paired in the same tooth with an assertion that a red packet's `failures` are byte-equal to the failures read back out of its own failing entries — because a complaint list passes either half alone; and a conformer deleted by mistake makes the record SHORTER by exactly the two lanes that could not run, with exactly ONE failing entry rather than one per lane.
owner: CC owns the code (cairn/machines/ruling/ + bin/cmd/ruling) and its proof, and gates writes to them. AKIEN OWNS CONFIRMATION, and since 2026-08-13 he holds it by typing RULED in his own words rather than by answering a question this component asked him — the door only READS his verbatim, and the recorder cannot author any of the five stamped fields (Law 6: the owner alone gates writes, and delegated confirmation is not confirmation). The earlier design put the gate on a second quote typed by the same hand that recorded the first, which is not a gate. The records are owned by the decisions store in CairnCommons; this is its intake door, not its owner.
traces_to: Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy — 'read his intent, not the code's shape' was policy all of 2026-07-31 and lost four times)
Law 3 (nothing is known until measured — the packet turns a heard ruling into a written claim that can be falsified in thirty seconds)
Law 7 (errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces — every refusal on the first pass, and a red ruling prints every turn until cleared)
Law 6 (Akien alone gates the confirm flag, and since 2026-08-13 he does it with a marker in his own words rather than by answering the gate's question)
Law 1 (a ruling becomes structure once; the resolver stops reconstructing it from the code)
memory akien-outranks-the-code (the feedback this component is the physics for)
provenance: Born 2026-07-31 out of the session's own failure, at the end of a day Akien described as 'a disaster… it's literally taken all day to get back to zero.' He named the shape of the fix as a question — 'should we just build the completely deterministic prebuild step to limit what opus tries to do?' — and ratified the narrowed version ('yes, do that') after it was scoped down from a full prebuild pipeline to a single gate at the one seam that had failed four times that day. THE FIRST PACKET THROUGH THE DOOR IS THIS RULING ITSELF (ruling 2026-07-31-the-ruling-intake-gate), opened before any of the files it names were edited, which is both the dogfood and the first real test that the door works outside its proof. THE FIRST CONFIRMATION FOUND THE NEXT DEFECT, minutes later: Akien typed `cairn ruling confirm <id>` into the session rather than into a shell, so the act was genuinely his while the keystroke was mine — and a bare `confirmed: true` could not tell those apart. Fixed before the flag was ever written: `confirm` now requires his words verbatim and records them beside `confirmed_by`, because a confirmation with no written source is precisely the failure this component exists to prevent, wearing this component's own clothes. THAT FIX WAS HALF OF ONE, and the other half took thirteen days and four refused asks to arrive: requiring his words verbatim did not stop the keystroke from being mine, so the second quote was as reconstructible as the first. 2026-08-13 finished it by deriving confirmation from a marker in the ruling itself — see filed edges (f) and (g). The component now asks him nothing.
learns: Yes; it accumulates rulings that become constraints — each ruling stored is a lesson learned.
